posts.bodyHtml:
I will never understand why so many poets hold up Rome burning to the ground across six days and seven nights as an example of how quickly we can be destroyed.

It only took me five seconds to decide to kill myself.

Like Poseidon, I stood howling at the foot of water I could never keep my head above. Every nurse in every emergency room across the world will tell you never to end your own life over a boy, but maybe it’s not so much over the boy, as what he did to you. And I was never over him, because I was always under him. His body, inside his bed, him taking what he felt he was owed.

He was Prometheus. He brought his own fire.

Maybe one day I will write a poem that will make him cry. That this closet I’ve filled with bells will one day stop ringing at the reminder of his voice. That ashes will not be an analogy to what I went through.

That one day I will not so much have gone through something as risen above it.

Someone once said God walked through mountains, that the Inuit have over one hundred and fifty words for snow. They say the most majestic creature is a horse with wings, because no one expects a body built for running to fly. So I will turn and face what I left behind; build my own language into something that the world will not dismiss as just another woman who was hurt.

If this is the eye of the storm, I will close its lids and move on.

posts.bodyHtml: it’s a huge huge huge fucking privilege to be vegan and i don’t mean solely monetarily i mean people that live in food deserts, people who work multiple jobs and don’t have access / time to prepare meals ahead of time or time to come home and cook, people with severe allergies or medical conditions that limit their food options, people whose food is more than just a meal but is their culture + their heritage, people who don’t have time or access to nutrition information. i think instead of turning veganism into another imperialist self serving endeavor we all need to focus on spreading information + resources + work towards building cooperative farms and food banks and make feeding our bodies wholly a possibility for everyone. we all know that factory farming and capitalism are evil, we already know that it is destroying our environment but your individual choices mean shit when all you’re contributing is alleviating your own guilt and guilting those without the same privileges you are awarded, we need to build community and understanding with one another we have to get our hands in the dirt and create

“Mara tells me that he was
no one special. Okay.
I believe her.
He was no one special.
Unremarkable, even.
A newspaper man with coffee
breath and ugly sneakers.
Mara tells me to let go.

But I waited for him, Mara.
I ate the scraps of his heart like
a starving dog under the dinner
table.
I slept at his feet and then by the
door when he was too far away.

I dreamt of coffee. I brought
the newspaper in every morning.

He was no one special, but it
didn’t matter, Mara,
because I kissed his stained teeth.
I brushed his unremarkable hair,
rested my head on his soft,
unremarkable stomach.

There was no hunger like my
hunger, Mara.
No man like my plain man.
No torch like my torch. ”
— Caitlyn Siehl, Unremarkable

t’s cute how men made it illegal for women to attend school or even learn to read, for actual millennia (and currently in many non-U.S. places, cf. Malala), and more recently stole their work in foundational disciplines like medicine, chemistry, computer science, and astrophysics – while also forbidding those women to seek legal recourse – and then discovered they had the balls to suggest that women are less intelligent than men and less inclined, by nature, to contribute to the sciences.

I have an idea! Let’s make it illegal for men to go to school, be represented in the courts and the legislature, and also drive them out of any field that doesn’t involve yelling loudly and killing each other with sharpened sticks. We’ll see how the innate innovative structures of the male mind adapt to those conditions after 4,000 years, ok? And then we’ll rehash this discussion and see how reasonable that ‘you problem’ looks.

posts.bodyHtml:
“A Love Affair
The sea loved the moon
When she was supposed to love the shore.

The moon knew
And hence made his intentions known.

That she should love the shore
Who was destined for her.

Yet his protests seemed weak.
And even when he pushed her towards the shore-
She always retreated back.

To want, to need, to love the moon
For all she’s worth.

Everyone said, it wasn’t meant to happen.
Yet, the Tsunami rose that night for their union.”
— Saiber, Stardust and Sheets
